_note: Pre-computed proposals for Constitution A (Privacy-First Productivity). Constitution B will produce different decisions at Step 3 live.

proposals.title: Offline-First Data Vault
proposals.description: Complete local-first architecture with encrypted offline storage, full metadata export, and optional end-to-end encrypted sync. All data lives on-device by default.
proposals.build_if: Target users (privacy-conscious knowledge workers) have explicitly stated offline access as a retention cliff. 78% enable offline mode within week 1. D30 retention gap: 85% vs 45%.
proposals.kill_because: Would require significant re-architecture if the product is currently cloud-first. But this aligns with every axis of Constitution A.

evidence_trail.quote: I need to own my data. Period.
78% of active users enable offline mode within first week. Retention: 85% vs 45%.
The app is useless without internet. Deleted it.
I love that my data stays on my device. Take my money.
If it doesn't work offline, I don't use it.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Implementation complexity of offline-first sync with conflict resolution may delay launch by 2+ months
early_signals: Engineer pushback on offline-first architecture complexity
untested_hypotheses: Users will tolerate occasional sync delays for data sovereignty
Local encryption doesn't impact performance on low-end devices
pre_mortem.mitigation: Ship offline storage without sync first (read-only offline). Add sync in v2.

feature_outline.target_user: Privacy-conscious knowledge workers who travel or work in low-connectivity environments
feature_outline.problem_statement: Users churn immediately when the app requires internet. 78% adopt offline mode when available, with 2x retention.
feature_outline.why_this_now: Retention cliff is the #1 growth blocker. Fixing this removes the biggest churn trigger.
supporting_feedback: obs-001: Data ownership is a hard requirement
obs-009: 85% vs 45% D30 retention with/without offline
obs-016: User deleted app due to no offline access
feature_outline.expected_outcome: D30 retention increases from 45% to 70%+ for currently cloud-only users
feature_outline.success_metric: D30 retention for new users reaches 75%

proposals.title: Evidence-Based Kill Reasoning Engine
proposals.description: Clause-level kill reasoning with evidence trail drill-down. Each kill decision shows which constitutional clause was violated, with direct observation quotes and pre-mortem diagnosis.
proposals.build_if: Core differentiation. Multiple senior PMs have expressed willingness to pay specifically for evidence-backed kill justification ($200/mo signal). This is the BONSAI differentiator.
proposals.kill_because: Only relevant if the constitution parser is accurate enough (H-4). If clause mapping is wrong, kill reasoning is wrong.

evidence_trail.quote: We need something that helps us explain why we're NOT building something.
Show me 12 pieces of evidence and 2 constitutional violations. That's what gets me political cover.
I'd pay $200/month if it could tell me which candidates to kill, with evidence.
If I can click on a kill decision and see the exact customer quotes, that's worth the subscription alone.
Never seen another tool that shows you what NOT to build with actual evidence.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Constitution parser accuracy below 70% (H-4 kill trigger), rendering all kill reasoning unreliable
early_signals: obs-027: User reports wrong clause mapping
obs-028: Constitution change doesn't change results
untested_hypotheses: 3-line constitution input provides enough signal for accurate 5-axis normalization
Clause-level reasoning is more persuasive than free-text explanation
pre_mortem.mitigation: Fall back to evidence-based reasoning without clause mapping if parser accuracy is insufficient. Pivot to dialog-based constitution extraction.

feature_outline.target_user: PMs and Heads of Product who need to justify kill/defer decisions to executives and stakeholders
feature_outline.problem_statement: Kill decisions are avoided because they're hard to justify. PMs say 'gut feeling' and get overruled. Evidence + clause violations make kills defensible.
feature_outline.why_this_now: AI overproduction is creating more candidates to evaluate. The need for systematic kill discipline is increasing week over week.
supporting_feedback: obs-006: Need to explain why we're NOT building something
obs-032: Evidence trail = political cover for difficult decisions
obs-008: $200/mo willingness to pay for evidence-based kills
feature_outline.expected_outcome: Time to make and defend kill decisions drops from 1 week to 10 minutes
feature_outline.success_metric: Users can make and justify a kill decision within a single session

proposals.title: Social Activity Feed
proposals.description: Real-time activity feed showing team members' actions, comments, and status updates. Includes @mentions, reactions, and activity notifications.
proposals.build_if: Target users wanted social engagement features. But they explicitly don't — 60% disable within 2 weeks, and adoption is only 12%.
proposals.kill_because: Directly violates Constitution A's prohibited_business_model (engagement-maximizing dark patterns) and quality_bar (simplicity over feature count). Evidence shows negative retention correlation.

evidence_trail.quote: Only 12% interact. 60% disable within 2 weeks. Top complaint: 'too noisy'.
Notification spam killed it. Engagement tricks don't work on people who want focus.
Don't add more features please.
Open rate: 8%. Click-through: 2%. Unsubscribe: 12% of MAU.

proposals.salvage_path: Strip to minimal 'decisions made this week' digest (obs-046 shows 45% open rate for weekly summary). Remove all real-time social features.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Social features attract the wrong user segment (engagement-seeking) while repelling the core segment (focus-seeking). Net negative retention impact.
early_signals: Negative correlation between social feature usage and NPS

proposals.title: AI Suggestion Panel (Proactive)
proposals.description: AI-powered contextual suggestions that proactively appear while the user is working. Suggests features, improvements, and actions based on current context.
proposals.build_if: Users wanted unsolicited AI assistance during their workflow. But usage data shows the opposite: retention is higher when the feature is disabled.
proposals.kill_because: Violates quality_bar (simplicity over feature count) and user trust. 45% initial click-through drops to 8% by day 7. Users who disable it have 14% higher retention. Unsolicited AI breaks deep focus flow.

evidence_trail.quote: 45% click-through drops to 8% by day 7. Users who disable have higher D30 retention (72% vs 58%).
The AI features feel forced. I didn't ask for suggestions. It breaks my flow.
It does one thing — helps me focus — and does it perfectly.

proposals.salvage_path: Convert from proactive push to on-demand pull. User explicitly requests AI analysis. Never interrupt flow.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Novelty effect masked the negative impact. Short-term engagement metrics looked good while long-term retention suffered.

proposals.title: Gamification & Achievement Badges
proposals.description: Achievement badges, streaks, and progress indicators to increase user engagement and daily active usage.
proposals.build_if: Target users valued gamified engagement. They don't. 5% adoption after 30 days with negative NPS correlation.
proposals.kill_because: Constitutional misalignment. Gamification is explicitly an engagement-maximizing pattern (forbidden_pattern) and contradicts quality_bar (simplicity). Users who interact with badges have 20% lower NPS.

evidence_trail.quote: 5% adoption after 30 days. Users who interact have 20% lower NPS. Negative correlation with focus_mode.
Engagement tricks don't work on people who want focus.
Finally a tool that doesn't try to do everything.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Gamification attracts engagement-seekers while repelling the core focus-oriented segment. Impossible to serve both.

proposals.title: Real-Time Team Collaboration Board
proposals.description: Live collaborative view of allocation decisions. Multiple PMs can view, discuss, and override build/kill decisions in real-time with role-based permissions.
proposals.build_if: Evidence is strong for teams >5 (88% adoption, 2.3x expansion revenue). But it conflicts with offline-first positioning — real-time requires always-online.
proposals.kill_because: Partial constitutional conflict. Real-time collaboration requires cloud-first architecture, which conflicts with Constitution A's strategic_terrain (offline-first). However, no hard clause violation — it's a tension, not a prohibition.

evidence_trail.quote: 92% of teams with 3+ members use it daily. 2.3x expansion revenue.
I want my team to collaborate in real-time.
Great for solo use but terrible for teams.
88% adoption in teams >5. Solo founders: 0%.

proposals.salvage_path: Implement async collaboration first (shared views, comment threads, decision history). Add real-time sync in v2 with offline-first conflict resolution.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Architectural tension between offline-first (Constitution A) and always-online collaboration. Choosing one alienates the other segment.
early_signals: Solo founders don't use collab features
Teams demand real-time but constitution requires offline-first
untested_hypotheses: Async collaboration is sufficient for teams <10
Offline-first teams accept eventual consistency for shared decisions
pre_mortem.mitigation: Offer both modes: offline-first with async sync for privacy segment, real-time for growth segment. Let constitution determine which mode is default.

proposals.title: Guided Constitution Builder
proposals.description: Interactive dialog that helps users write their constitution through a series of targeted questions instead of blank 3-line input. Includes templates and examples.
proposals.build_if: Onboarding data shows 32% drop-off at constitution input step. One user spent 45 minutes and gave up. Guided input could dramatically improve conversion.
proposals.kill_because: No hard clause violation. But the evidence for guided input is mixed — it might hand-hold too much and produce generic constitutions. The current 3-line approach may filter for the right users (founders with strong product vision).

evidence_trail.quote: Biggest drop: constitution_input → first_pipeline_run.
Writing 'We are / We never / We value' took me 45 minutes.
The naming is too academic. Just call it 'product policy'.

proposals.salvage_path: Start with 3 industry-specific templates (SaaS, Consumer, Dev Tools). Add guided dialog in v2 if template adoption > 50%.

pre_mortem.death_cause: Guided builder produces generic constitutions that all look the same, eliminating the differentiation that constitution-based reasoning provides.
early_signals: Template-generated constitutions all produce similar allocations
Users skip questions in the guided flow
untested_hypotheses: Users prefer templates over blank input
Guided constitutions are as effective as hand-written ones
pre_mortem.mitigation: Keep both paths: guided for new users, raw input for power users. Track which path produces higher-quality allocations.
